BOWERS MUSEUM
CALIFORNIA BOUNTY
___
By Joy Z.
Untitled (Still Life, Tangerines) by Alberta Binford McCloskey (1889)
INTRODUCTION
Inside Bowers Museum in Santa Ana, California, ancient civilizations come to life and so does
the history of California. Most drawings from the California Bounty section are works by early
artists documenting the Mission and Rancho periods, and of those are two famous artists
Alberta Binford and William Joseph McCloskey.
ALBERTA BINFORD & WILLIAM MCCLOSEKEY
Although when the painting of Oranges in Tissues with Vase was ﬁrst discovered, nothing was
known about the two artists except for the signature of “William J. McCloskey.”, the experts
were confused because the quality of the painting was so high. Through newspapers and
researchers, they ﬁnally unveiled a story between two talented artists. Their time for
2
recognition came around 100 years after their time, with auction prices for the still lifes of
oranges climbing to hundreds of thousands of dollars.
TOGETHER
Alberta Binford and William McClosekey ﬁrst met in 1882 or 1883, in Denver, Colorado, after
Alberta had separated from her family in Los Angeles. William had also just arrived recently
from Philadelphia, who studied with Thomas Eakins at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine
Arts. They were both talented artists in a small town, the two fell instantly in love and were
married in March 1883. Around a year later, their baby Eleanor was welcomed into the world.
She quickly became a frequent subject in many of McClosekey’s paintings, with as many as
thirty, all of them from before her 10th birthday.
The McClosekey family traveled quite frequently, and in the early summer of 1884, they decided
to move to Los Angeles, California, where Alberta reconciled with her family. While they
seemingly prospered in Los Angeles, they traveled to New York in 1886, these were only the ﬁrst
cross-country trips they have made. Throughout these trips, the couple had made several
exhibitions and lent their artworks.
SEPARATION
Around 1898, the couple separated, although there was no record of divorce. Alberta stayed in
San Francisco with their two children, Eleanor and William, Jr. William returned home to his
family in Philadelphia. Even after their separation, Alberta remains a successful career as a
single mother.
